comparisons.peer_topic: Credit and Funding Spread Sensitivity on Derivatives and Liabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Sensitivity to a one basis point increase in credit and funding spreads on derivatives resulted in a $2 million loss in 2024 and 2023, while sensitivity to own credit spreads on elected fair value financial liabilities resulted in gains of $43 million and $42 million respectively, subject to liquidity and hedge performance factors.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose the financial sensitivity of their financial liabilities to changes in their own credit spreads. MS defines the metric as the potential gain for a 1 basis point widening of its credit spread, while GS quantifies the estimated gain from a 1 basis point increase in its own credit spreads on fair value elected liabilities ($43 million in 2024). GS additionally notes that this sensitivity applies to financial liabilities where the fair value option was elected and is influenced by liquidity and hedge performance.

sentences.text: 1.Amounts represent the potential gain for each 1 bps widening of our credit spread.

In addition, the estimated sensitivity to a one basis point increase in our own credit spreads on financial liabilities for which the fair value option was elected was a gain of $43 million as of December 2024 and $42 million as of December 2023.

However, the actual net impact of a change in our own credit spreads is also affected by the liquidity, duration and convexity (as the sensitivity is not linear to changes in yields) of those financial liabilities for which the fair value option was elected, as well as the relative performance of any hedges undertaken.
